sections.html:
Lakewood is a township in Ocean County and the county's most populous municipality, with 143,765 people in the 2025 estimate, up from 135,158 in 2020. Growth has been fast since the 1960s, when woods and cranberry bogs gave way to subdivisions. Parcels range from older single-family lots near the lakes to newer builds and large condominium communities, so two houses a few blocks apart can carry very different assessments.

The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $466,700 and median gross rent is $1,774. About 51.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, which leaves roughly half rented, so many sellers here are landlords with tenants in place. A buyer will ask for the lease, the rent roll and any open repair requests, and unpaid tax on a rental parcel creates the same lien risk as on an owner-occupied one.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in the Municipal Building
sections.html:
Two desks inside the Municipal Building at 231 Third Street, Lakewood, NJ 08701, split the work. The Tax Assessor fixes the assessed value of each parcel, while the Tax Collector mails the bill and receives payment. The county tax board in Toms River hears assessment appeals.

  • Tax Assessor: 732-364-2500, extension 5248, open 8:30 AM to 5 PM. Ownership records, name and address changes and senior, disability and veteran deduction forms go through this office.
  • Tax Collector: 732-364-2500, open 9 AM to 5 PM. Bring payment questions, payoff requests and tax sale concerns to this desk.
  • Ocean County Board of Taxation: receives appeals at the Courthouse on Washington Street in Toms River.

A new deed reaches the tax records when the Ocean County Clerk forwards it to the assessor, and the collector then works from the assessor's file. If a closing is close, ask the assessor to confirm the owner of record so the bill and any payoff request go to the right name.

sections.h2: Due dates and late payment costs
sections.html:
Lakewood taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. The township gives a 10-day grace period, so a payment that reaches the office by the 10th carries no interest. Days are counted from the date the township receives payment, and a postmark does not help.

Bills go out once a year in the summer with four coupons. The first two quarters equal half of the prior year's bill, and the last two reflect the rate struck for the current year, so they come out larger if the rate rose and smaller if it fell. You owe the tax even if no bill reaches you, and escrow with a lender does not change that.

Lakewood late-payment charges
ChargeRateApplies to
Interest8% a yearFirst $1,500 of a delinquency
Interest18% a yearEvery dollar over $1,500
Year-end penalty6%Open tax and interest above $10,000 on December 31, after which the whole amount accrues at 18% from January 1

A balance counts as current once all earlier bills are paid before the next quarter comes due.

sections.h2: What a payoff looks like at a sale
sections.html:
A Lakewood house can be sold with tax owed, because the closing agent pays the open amount out of the seller's proceeds and records the payment. The seller needs a figure from the collector that runs through the closing date, including any accrued interest.

The bigger concern is a tax sale lien. Lakewood holds a tax sale each year for the previous year's unpaid municipal charges, which covers water, sewer, maintenance liens and taxes. Selling at a tax sale does not transfer the house. A lien goes on the parcel instead, and the buyer of that lien earns interest until it is redeemed.

Most lienholders record the lien with the Ocean County Clerk, and clear title cannot be issued while a recorded lien sits on the property. Liens must be redeemed in full with guaranteed funds. A lien held by the township allows foreclosure to begin six months after the sale, and a lien bought by a third party allows it after two years. If you see a certificate on the parcel, ask the collector for the redemption amount before listing or signing a contract.

Owners challenge the assessed value, never the tax itself, and the deadline falls on April 1 of the year at issue. A filing counts only when it arrives at the Ocean County Board of Taxation, so mail or drop it off with time to spare. The township cannot accept a petition meant for the county board.

The assessor mails a postcard notice on or before February 1 showing land, building and total value along with the prior year's tax. The practical limits of an appeal:

  • Land and building values cannot be appealed separately.
  • Assessments of neighboring houses are not accepted as evidence of your value.
  • The first quarter's taxes and municipal charges must be paid before the appeal can be completed.
  • Skipping a certificate of occupancy does not avoid an assessment.

The assessor's office will review a value with an owner by appointment before any filing. The burden of proof sits with the owner, who should attach three to five comparable sales, and a county board decision can be taken to the Tax Court within 45 days.

State programs help eligible owners, and the township assessor's office handles the local deductions: the senior citizen deduction, the disability deduction, the surviving spouse deduction, the veteran deductions and the disabled veteran exemption. The forms are in the township's download center.

The fiscal year 2027 state budget funds the Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ programs. Their application windows run yearly, so check the Division of Taxation relief page for the next one. The state also warns against clicking links in unsolicited texts or emails about relief benefits.

A sale can change eligibility, so a seller who receives a benefit should ask the state program office how a mid-year move affects the claim.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell a Lakewood house
sections.html:
Work through the tax side in this order. Confirm the owner of record with the assessor. Ask the collector for the balance by quarter and whether any lien certificate sits on the parcel. If you disagree with your value, remember the April 1 cutoff and that the petition goes to Toms River, not to the township. Before the closing date, request an updated written payoff, since interest shifts the number every day.

Landlords should gather leases and rent records, and anyone selling an inherited property should bring the paperwork that shows who owns it now. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, but the closing agent still has to pay the tax payoff and any lien before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What is the Lakewood property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year being appealed, and the petition must be received by the Ocean County Board of Taxation in Toms River. A petition handed to the township does not count.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Lakewood house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Your closing agent requests a payoff from the Lakewood tax collector and pays the balance from your sale proceeds. If a tax sale certificate already exists on the parcel, the lien must be redeemed in full with guaranteed funds before clear title can pass.

faqs.q: How much interest does Lakewood charge on late taxes?
faqs.a: Interest runs at 8% a year on the first $1,500 of delinquency and 18% on the amount above that. A 6% year-end penalty applies when open tax and interest on December 31 exceed $10,000.

faqs.q: Which Lakewood office explains my assessed value?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Assessor at 732-364-2500, extension 5248, in the Municipal Building at 231 Third Street. The office reviews values by appointment on weekdays between 8:30 AM and 5 PM.

faqs.q: Why is my Lakewood second-half tax bill different from the first half?
faqs.a: The first two quarters are set at half of last year's bill, while the last two reflect the rate struck for the current year. If the budgets of the county, school district and township rose, the second half grows, and if they fell it shrinks.
